stem: In addition to the left pale optic disc, an eye review in this patient is likely to reveal which of the following?

options.text: Cherry red spots of the macula

explanation: This child has neurofibromatosis type 1, suggested by multiple café au lait macules, macrocephaly, developmental differences, and an optic glioma. A classic ophthalmic finding in NF1 is Lisch nodules of the iris.
rationale: The clinical picture is neurofibromatosis type 1; Lisch nodules are a common associated ocular feature.

optionExplanations.A: Cherry red spots are seen in retinal disorders such as Tay-Sachs disease, not NF1.
optionExplanations.B: Lens opacities are not a typical feature of NF1.
optionExplanations.C: Lisch nodules are iris hamartomas and are a classic eye finding in neurofibromatosis type 1.
optionExplanations.D: Papilloedema suggests raised intracranial pressure and is not the characteristic associated eye finding here.

Instructions

Question 6 - 8 relate to this case

Case 3

A 4 year old girl is brought in to see you because her ‘birth marks’ have been increasing in number and they are starting to concern her mother. The child is the 2nd to non-consanguineous Italian parents. She was born with 4 birth marks on her abdomen and back which are light brown in colour. Over the last 2 years her family have noted that they are increasing in number and size and she now has at least a dozen spots. The child is otherwise well, she has just started pre-school and although her language skills are not as advanced as other children, she is able to keep up with them in all other aspects.

On examination she is not dysmorphic. Her head circumference is 52cm (98th centile), weight is 15kg (50th centile) and her height is 95cm (10th centile). Her BP is 90/70 (normal). Her skin has 10 café au lait macules and 8 of them are over 5cm in diameter. There are no other skin findings. Her gait is normal. On cranial nerve examination you estimate her visual acuity to be 6/60 on the left but 6/6 on the right. Her visual fields are also restricted over the right side. Her pupils are normal but optic atrophy is present on the left. The rest of her cranial nerves are normal. She has normal tone, power and reflexes.

An MRI of the brain depicts an intraorbital mass on the left that contrast enhances and is consistent with an optic glioma.
